scope: Live reread of the prior selected 1,160 Current source paths, excluding Workbench/Workflow-named source files or active Subjects. No Current or code writes.
findings: 42 exact Relation-descriptor active Subjects each have one Requirement/Declaration in the bounded source set. 29 explicitly Direct, two explicitly Derived, 11 minimal inverse declarations are Derived by their reciprocal HAS_INVERSE binding; both sides of each recorded inverse pair are present.

36 actual named Relation operators observed in bounded fenced CFEL have an exact descriptor Declaration. Generic ((RELATION)) and Relation//RELATION_NAME are syntax placeholders declared by R2609/R2613 and R2720, respectively; do not create Relations for them.

BLOCKS R1580 is Derived and IS_BLOCKED_BY R2762 Direct; directions and reciprocal inverse bindings match the latest decision. IS_DECLARED_BY R2732 is a qualified reversed GOVERNS view, not an unconditional inverse. Minimal inverse binding does not grant its own outgoing permission; R2588 explicitly requires separate effective permission.

Descriptor inventory records each source pin, classification, reciprocal binding, declared aliases and full formal CFEL Claims. Relation//NAME denotes a descriptor; ((NAME)) in signatures denotes the named Relation. No declaration contains a cardinality placed on a named Relation descriptor as if it were an endpoint.

CA-E-383@Current and CA-M-232@Current describe opposite named views as requiring the named derived inverse; this omits the independent <((RELATION)) reverse-written view admitted by CA-R-2609 and CA-R-1931, including where no named inverse exists. Route both wording corrections to the expression-syntax lane; no duplicate previews were created here.

An additional full-text named-delimiter scan of the same bounded sources found only NAME, R, RELATION and RELATION_TYPE unmatched; these occur as generic notation placeholders, not named Relation types.
limitations: The prior selected frontier is a bounded source selection, not an all-live census. This pass scans fenced CFEL operators; prose-only, dynamic/wildcard names, plugin/code surfaces, and excluded Workbench/Workflow sources are not proven complete.
Generic endpoint signatures do not themselves prove kinds/populations or effective inherited permissions. A declared signature is not an independent outgoing permission or runtime evidence.
Classification, inverse bindings and CFEL clauses are source observations; unsupported runtime/projection enforcement is not inferred. No Workflow source or semantics was modified.
